title: Fun Classroom Commands!
summary: Practise simple instructions we use in English lessons.
keyIdeas: Commands tell us which action to do.
Stand up means rise to your feet. Sit down means take a seat.
We say please to ask politely.

activities.prompt: The teacher says, 'Sit down, please.' What do you do?
activities.explanation: Sit down means take a seat on your chair.
activities.hint: Think about what you do at your desk.

activities.prompt: The command 'Stand up!' means '¡Ponte de pie!' in Spanish.
activities.explanation: Stand up tells us to rise to our feet. Its Spanish meaning is '¡Ponte de pie!'.

activities.prompt: Match each English command to its Spanish meaning.
activities.explanation: Listen means escuchar; look means mirar; silence, please means silencio, por favor; and clap your hands means aplaudir.

activities.prompt: The teacher wants us to start reading. Complete the command.
activities.explanation: Open your book asks you to open it. In Spanish, this is 'Abre tu libro'.
activities.hint: It is the opposite of closing.

activities.prompt: We play Simon Says! Simon says, 'Touch your nose!' What do you touch?
activities.explanation: Touch your nose asks you to put a finger on your nose.
activities.hint: Find the part of your face used for smelling.

activities.prompt: Sort these instructions into the right group.
activities.explanation: Jump, stand up and clap your hands are body actions. Opening and closing refer to the book in these examples.

activities.prompt: Class has finished, and we put our things away. Complete the sentence.
activities.explanation: Close your book means 'Cierra tu libro' in Spanish.
activities.hint: Think of the opposite of open.

activities.prompt: Put these instructions in order for the start of class.
activities.explanation: In this routine, we come in, sit down and then open our books.

activities.prompt: In PE, the teacher says, 'Stop!' What does Omar do?
activities.explanation: Stop means stop moving and stay still straight away.
activities.hint: Think of a red traffic light.

activities.prompt: Read the story and answer the questions.
activities.explanation: The story tells us which instructions Miss Sarah gives in class.
activities.title: Aisha in English Class
activities.text: Miss Sarah is in class. She says: 'Good morning! Sit down, please.' Aisha sits down. Miss Sarah says: 'Open your book and look.' Aisha opens her book. Then Miss Sarah says: 'Listen to the story.' Aisha is quiet and happy.

questions.prompt: What does Miss Sarah tell Aisha to do first?
questions.explanation: Her first instruction is 'Sit down, please'.

questions.prompt: What does Miss Sarah tell Aisha to open?
questions.explanation: She says 'Open your book and look', so Aisha opens her book.
